e: The trial of Russell Brand begins, having been delayed from June after further charges were brought.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood announces that political figures who are not serving MPs will be provided with police support.
A health and safety investigation is launched into the death of a man in the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.
CrossCountry announces plans for an extra 60,000 train seats each week, with eight additional services.
The UK government launches a new taskforce to respond to extreme weather conditions, such as flooding.
Burnham tells The Rest Is Politics podcast that it was "clear" Russia had interfered in the 2016 Brexit vote.
A man is killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park after he entered the animal's enclosure.
In a letter to the National Cyber Security Centre, The King warns of the challenges posed by disinformation and other "hostile online activity" to trust and security in the digital age.
James Deller is dismissed as the Metropolitan Police head of Special Constabulary after Palantir's AI monitoring uncovered that he had used his work phone to copy intimate images of a woman.
It emerges that The King has paid Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's £1.5m repair bill for the maintenance of his former home at Royal Lodge in Windsor.
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant announces he will ban the contentious Orange Order parade at Drumcree.
Holborn and St Pancras by-election: Labour retain the seat, with Camden council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali elected as the constituency's MP.
At the Green Party conference, members back a 'Zionism is racism' motion.
The British Museum announces changes to how visitors see the Bayeux Tapestry to ease long queueing times, including later opening hours, audio tours and more seating.

Trump withdraws all US bombers from RAF Fairford, an air base targeted by an attack that the UK linked to the Iranian government, due to urgent concerns about a potentially complex drone attack ordered by the IRGC as part of a plot to target the aircraft and kill American soldiers at RAF Fairford, loosely modelled after Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb.
Wakefield Trinity win the 2026 Super League Grand Final after defeating Warrington Wolves 23–10.
The price of diesel in the UK exceeds £2/litre for the first time, as the Iran war continues to put pressure on supplies.
A suspect in the killing of Ann Widdecombe is charged with plotting a terrorist attack against Nigel Farage.
Two Iranian nationals are charged with terrorist offences relating to a targeted plot against Manchester's Jewish community.

Around 700 prisoners are released from prisons in England and Wales as new early-release rules under the Sentencing Act 2026 come into force. The changes allow many prisoners serving standard determinate sentences to be released after serving a smaller proportion of their custodial term.
A new excise duty on vaping products comes into force across the UK, charging £2.20 per 10 ml of vaping liquid, including products without nicotine.
The yield on 30-year UK government bonds exceeds 6% for the first time since 1998, amid a global bond sell-off and continuing inflationary pressure from the Iran war.

A 25-year-old dual UK-Iranian national becomes the sixth person arrested in connection with the suspected terrorist activity near RAF Fairford, on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. Counter Terrorism Policing says it is investigating possible foreign state involvement.
Burnham tells BBC Radio 4's Today programme that Brexit has caused "more harm than good" and that the UK should consider "options" to clarify its relationship with Europe.

The Metropolitan Police submits its final investigation files into the 2017 Grenfell Tower fire to the Crown Prosecution Service, relating to 54 individuals and 20 companies and organisations. Potential charges include corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, health and safety offences, fraud and misconduct in public office.
Burnham says the UK government believes Iran played a part in the incident at RAF Fairford.
The UK government announces the "one in, one out" agreement with France allowing the UK to return some migrants to France has been scrapped.
Greggs announces plans to close four of its factories with the loss of 740 jobs.
Following his conviction on 24 August, former snooker world champion Graeme Dott is sentenced at Edinburgh's high court to seven years in prison for sexually abusing two children.

Burnham tells the Labour Party Conference that the government will end the pensions "triple lock" and instead move to a "double lock" by 2030. He also announces a new "national care service", as well as plans for electoral reform, an overhaul of the leasehold system for housing, and greater public ownership of water companies.
The Premier League confirms that Manchester City F.C. has been found guilty of breaching its rules, including arranging sham contracts with its commercial partners.
The UK government announces that the universal free admission policy of England's national museums will not be changed.
The RAC reports that diesel has reached an all-time high of 199.18p per litre, as the ongoing Iran war continues to push up prices. Petrol has also risen further, with a litre now at 174.13p.
The UK government announces that train operator Avanti West Coast will be nationalised from March 2027.
Merseyside Police arrest 50 pro-Palestine Action protesters outside the Labour Party Conference.
Prior to the Orange walk, protesters block a Catholic area in Portadown.

A major incident is declared near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, after several men were arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and committing offences under the Explosives Act. Residents in the nearby village of Whelford are evacuated to a leisure centre while investigations continue.
Burnham announces plans for a National Care Service as part of Labour's manifesto at the next general election.
Ten NHS staff are to be removed or suspended from their posts following a data breach involving the medical records of Noah Woods.
Detectives are granted an extra week to question two men arrested on suspicion of planning a terrorist attack against Manchester's Jewish community.
